modules.role: the USB end: the Type-C receptacle with its two CC pulldowns (R1/R2), the VBUS reservoir C2 and the VBUS lamp D1+R3, drawn first because the reader enters the sheet from the connector side

the middle: the CH343G bridge U1 alone — its own real designator and value rows and the VCC/GND flags it must hang need the room that C1/C3 were taking; every signal it carries still leaves the island for one of the others, so the boundary nets are all cross-island labels

U1's own supply decoupling, one island: C1 the 100nF on VDD5 (the +5V rail U1.16 feeds), C3 the 100nF on V3 (the regulator output U1.4 makes) and C4 the 100nF on VCC/VIO (the level rail H1.9 exposes); all three are shunt capacitors from a rail to GND, none is a USB supply and none is a placement claim

the far end: the 2x5 header alone, carrying the eight UART/MODEM lines plus the VCC level rail and GND, where the peer board attaches; C4 was drawn here only because VCC enters the sheet here and now has its own island

directWiringObligations.note: the VBUS lamp's cathode and R3 are one conductor inside the usb_c island: labelPolicy.local is 'wire', so naming the lamp's return would be a label where the policy promises a wire (534; the pair is D1 pin 2 to R3 pin 1, nothing else on the net)

localLabelObligations.note: Type-C 可逆引脚交错: the receptacle's data pins are mirrored pairs, D+ on USB1.A6/B6 and D- on USB1.A7/B7, so one wire inside usb_c would have to tie the two halves of a pair and draw a U-line that presents one pin as the other; instead each of the four pins takes its own short stub and the golden board's same-name label (D+ on A6 and B6, D- on A7 and B7), and the pair reaches U1.5/U1.6 by the same-named labels there — the name carries the net, no U-line does
